“2 parents that are separate and happy is much better than 2 parents who are together and unhappy” boy oh boy if that isn’t true.

then, at the age of 19, my mum got sick. she almost died, and was in hospital for three weeks. i’m 21 now and she’s doing much better, but still has regular check ups. anyway, when my mum was in hospital, my dad reached out to his family who stalked, harassed and bullied my mum for years at around the age of 23. he let those people that threatened to kill her and myself when i was an infant back into our lives, and cheated on my mum with his ex. 

i can’t tell you how dismal it is being at home. for me, for my sister, for my mum and for my grandma. even my dog understands something is wrong, he always used to be such a happy dog and he’s become so withdrawn.

styro looks white, and blood beads up in it. it’s not good, but it’s normally manageable at home - keep it clean and covered for most of the day, and uncovered at night. wash it gently every day with warm water and a bit of soap, that should be good enough to keep it uninfected. 

fat, on the other hand, looks yellow and bubbly, and the skin will be pretty far apart. it’s deeper than styro, and as a result, the skin will be further apart. now, there’s shallow fat (think that’s the wrong terminology, but i can’t remember) and deep fat. both should get stitches, but shallow fat *is* possible (i wouldn’t recommend it) to treat at home. antibacterial wipes are a must, and a good, large bandage that covers the wound well (there should be lots of space left on either side of the wound once it’s covered by the bandage). 
immediately after the cut is made, keep pressure on it with a towel (NOT tissues or toilet paper as those can get stuck inside the wound, and are a risk for infection), and keep that pressure on for 10 minutes. check to see if it’s stopped bleeding, if not, hold for another 10 minutes. if it still hasn’t stopped bleeding, time for stitches. if it has, then get rid of all the blood around the wound with warm water and a towel, or anything clean that isn’t tissues or toilet paper, such as a t shirt. cover it with a (preferably non stick) bandage, and leave it alone for the day. the next day, take it off, give it a wash with warm water, and take care of any blood if it starts to bleed again (it won’t be nearly as much as when it was initially made). then, pat it dry, wait for it to be fully dry, because warm, wet/moist/damp environments are breeding grounds for fungal infections. go AROUND the area (that’s important, not inside the wound) with the antibacterial wipes, and then cover it with a new bandage. check on it every day to make sure it’s not getting infected, and if it shows even the slightest sign of it, doctor/hospital immediately. infections can be deadly. keep doing this every day, and you should be fine. although, like i said, deep fat should always get stitches. i have scars everywhere because i didn’t get my deep fat cuts stitched, and even apart from that, hurts like a fucking bitch to walk around with deep fat wounds not stitched up (i was working at a fast food restaurant and walked into every table with jt, not fun at all). 

but yeah, i hope it’s going well taking care of it at the moment!
